Implementation update · 6 September 2026

Report audit remediation.

Implementation changes address all 28 findings below: saved identities and source revisions, acknowledged writes, durable accounting, predictable replay, clearer evaluation semantics and bounded work.

The original audit is preserved below. Its findings and line references describe the pre-fix source. This update records remediation, not a claim that every failure scenario has been reproduced and retested.

Implementation details, compatibility changes and validation limits

What changed

FindingImplemented behavior
R01Stable score identity
Rerank rows join saved source Agent IDs before projection into the current answer order. Removed or reordered participants cannot relabel a surviving score.
R02Replay model identity
Full replay builds tasks from the saved provider/model and Agent row ID, including when the live Agent now points elsewhere.
R03Acknowledged saves
Report and secondary writes fail explicitly. The UI retains unsaved JSON for retry or copying; retries merge against newer disk state and refuse conflicting changes.
R04Independent accounting
Report ledger recording runs before the optional aggregate-statistics toggle, so disabling statistics no longer suppresses Report accounting.
R05Durable cost queue
Every captured call gets a UUID journal record. A trailing flush appends deduplicated records; failed writes retain pending data for the next flush.
R06Rejected worker costs
Usage from paid but rejected worker outputs and fixed-judge parse failures is recorded. Primary and secondary usage accounting occurs before saving the answer.
R07Orphan-Agent completion
Deleted Agents retain their original report row identity on replay. Unresolvable providers become explicit errors instead of leaving unmatched pending tasks.
R08Saved execution settings
Primary attempts persist resolved prompt, parameters and endpoint. Batch manifests preserve expanded workers, prompt settings and runtime Tournament temperature for replay. Credentials stay live references.
R09Original analysis inputs
Immutable source snapshots preserve answer text and participant identity. Translation reviews freeze original and translated passages. Unknown or changed revisions are labelled historical and excluded from current-answer comparisons.
R10Retry and scheduling semantics
Primary work precedes optional metadata. Retry skips successful siblings, waits for submitted work to settle, and directly retries unfinished rows. Stop scheduling explicitly allows submitted calls to finish and incur cost.
R11Empty scopes
Empty Manual and Top Ranked selections remain empty instead of expanding to all answers.
R12Local control contract
Local requests include resolved system instructions and apply supported temperature, top-p, top-k and seed controls. Unsupported controls and non-default context overrides produce explicit errors.
R13Worker control scope
Workers resolve prompt, bound-Agent and app defaults before dispatch; frozen worker configuration is used by batch retries. The UI no longer claims primary controls govern every call.
R14Shared knowledge context
One retrieval result is saved and reused for the report answers. Configuration/retrieval failures stop grounded generation with an explicit error; empty successful retrieval is distinguished.
R15Portable export redaction
Single-report bundles and bulk archives redact credential fields, authorization headers, bearer tokens and sensitive URL parameters, including embedded legacy diagnostic JSON.
R16Transactional Report bundles
ZIP entries are streamed into bounded staging, validated and remapped. Evidence and secondary files commit before the parent report; a journal rolls back interrupted imports. Every final write is checked.
R17Duplicate preference
Report duplication carries metadataDisabled, preserving the saved metadata opt-out.
R18Distinct Agent variants
Selection deduplicates configured Agents by Agent identity and direct models by provider/model. Two Agent roles on one model remain separate report rows.
R19Explicit group provenance
Group parameters and system prompts follow the selected Flock/Swarm source; unrelated group membership no longer changes a direct pick.
R20Meaningful value display
The chart highlights all priced Pareto-frontier options and removes the arbitrary quality/cost-ratio winner. Current answer cost is separate from cumulative and fan-out spend.
R21Evidence families and coverage
Tournament methods share one evidence-family contribution. Combined requires common coverage across informative families and excludes translation ability from original-answer quality. Ignored translation-weight controls were removed.
R22Independent judge agreement
Agreement excludes the judge being evaluated and requires a unique plurality from at least two other distinct judges. The UI reports the eligible sample count and unavailable evidence.
R23Translation review limits
Sampling spreads the capped judge cells over passages; aggregation weights passages equally. The interface describes a translation review and explains that differing passages/judges are not a controlled benchmark.
R24Honest wording cues
English lexical heuristics are labelled Wording cues and Refusal wording, with unknown states and limitations for quotation, negation and other languages.
R25Attempt cost and estimates
Current-attempt usage and cost are stored separately from lifetime spend. Estimated usage is flagged in Matrix/Value/cost displays; replacing answer text clears obsolete attribution.
R26Bounded work and storage
Large answer/request strings use immutable content files, keeping frequent parent writes smaller. Report caches and coroutine windows are bounded; oversized batches and import archives are rejected. Bulk exports materialize the text.
R27Producer and action labels
Manage and Matrix show model identity alongside generated titles. Score-against-meta wording distinguishes the scoring operation from prose comparison.
R28Work review and limits
Shared preflight shows item count and request allowance, plus an optional recorded-cost stop. The HTTP interceptor reserves requests durably, including retries and metadata; a batch is limited to 5,000 items.

Validation: Kotlin compilation, full debug build, emulator installation with existing data retained, cloud APK copy, and manual checks of an existing Report and its historical-source warning. Local fixture results are recorded in the linked remediation notes. Unit/instrumented suites, paid provider calls, and destructive fault injection were not run.

Old inputs or unrecorded costs cannot be reconstructed. Save recovery requires keeping the app open until writing succeeds or the payload is copied. Spend stops can be exceeded by submitted calls; bounded queues and storage changes still need workload profiling.

Android multi-provider AI · Report feature

Original audit assessment.

Report is a sophisticated analysis workspace. Its most urgent weaknesses are in proving which answer was evaluated, which configuration produced it, and which costs were durably recorded.

The feature has substantial safeguards and the current source builds successfully. Nevertheless, ordinary actions such as changing an Agent, removing an answer, retrying a run, or disabling statistics can break the relationship between visible results and their provenance. Evaluation labels then add a second risk: presenting agreement, heuristics, and relative scores as stronger evidence than they are.

28Findings, including design risks
6P1 · high-priority integrity issues
20P2 · defects, contracts & measurement
2P3 · usability & planning

Recommended first move: establish immutable answer/run identities, make persistence acknowledge actual durable writes, and separate report accounting from optional statistics. Fix identity joins before polishing rankings or adding more analysis modes.

No P0 is established. This audit identifies serious conditional failures, not evidence that all existing reports are corrupt. The 28 entries include confirmed source defects, documented-but-surprising behavior, measurement limitations, and one explicitly unmeasured scaling risk.

Counts include all lines, including comments and blanks. Review depth was concentrated on Report’s consequential paths, not an assertion that every line in every file received equal scrutiny.

  • PASS: JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@25 ./gradlew :ai:assembleDebug. Build successful in 24 seconds; 39 actionable tasks, 15 executed and 24 up to date.
  • PASS: emulator boot, installed com.ai launch, foreground confirmation, and read-only navigation through Manage → Second results → View.

Boundaries and confidence

No paid AI generation, report modification/deletion, import/export of real credentials, disk-full injection, process-death fault test, unit suite, or instrumented suite was run. Repository instructions reserve the extended test cycle for an explicit request. The build and read-only walkthrough were appropriate for this audit-only change; application source and installed data were not intentionally modified.

The referenced external memory files were absent at their documented paths; the repository’s supplied AGENTS.md cycle instructions were used. Existing tests were inventoried and representative relevant source examined, but this audit makes no numerical test-coverage claim.

“Code defect” means a concrete causal path in the current source, with the proposed trigger stated separately from tests actually executed. “Workflow contract” means implementation behavior conflicts with an exposed or reasonable user expectation. “Measurement limitation” means a number’s interpretation is weaker than its apparent decision value. “Unmeasured risk” requires profiling before claiming a device-performance failure.

Severity: P1 = prioritize promptly because identity, durability, accounting, or historical interpretation can be wrong; P2 = material conditional defect, control mismatch, or analysis limitation; P3 = useful workflow improvement. Severity is an audit judgment, not a CVSS score.

P1R01

Rerank scores can move to the wrong answers

Evaluation · Code defect · Source review; scenario not run end to end

Value, Combined, and Answer Matrix can identify the wrong model as the strongest answer after the successful-answer set changes. This is silent corruption of the decision presented to the user.

Trigger / reproduction scenario
Create successful answers A, B, C, then rerank them as IDs 1, 2, 3. Delete A, or make an earlier failed answer successful. Reopen Value or Matrix. The current successful list is renumbered, but the original rerank IDs are reused.
Evidence and causal chain
Value loads only parsed rerank content and buildValuePoints indexes it with idx + 1 from the current successful agents. Combined similarly consumes numerical rerank IDs. Matrix loads the same numerical map and looks up rankRows[ordinal]. The secondary already stores sourceAgentIds, and resolveTopRankedAgents/sourceAgentLabels demonstrate an identity-aware implementation elsewhere. Removing an answer does not remove all its historical reranks. Example: original A=90, B=60, C=20 becomes displayed B=90, C=60 after A is removed.
Recommended change
Resolve every ranking entry through the run’s saved sourceAgentIds, then join by stable answer ID. Do not infer identity from current list position. Preserve a missing participant as a historical participant or exclude it explicitly. Also address answer revisions under R09.
Verification to run after a fix
Acceptance: rerank A/B/C; delete A; B must retain 60 and C 20 in Value, Combined, and Matrix. Repeat with a failed answer becoming successful, reordered rows, and an imported report.

P1R02

Full regeneration can call model B and save it under model A

Regeneration · Code defect · Source review; scenario not run end to end

A report can misstate which provider/model produced a regenerated answer. The response and its spend can be attached to a row labeled with the old model, undermining comparisons and provenance.

Trigger / reproduction scenario
Generate a report from a saved Agent configured for A. Edit that Agent, keeping its UUID, to use B. Run full agent regeneration. This differs from regenerating one persisted answer directly.
Evidence and causal chain
reportToModels resolves a surviving Agent UUID against current settings. forceRegenerateAllAgents rebuilds runtime tasks from those current Agents but resets/writes existing rows by resultId. updateAgentStatus updates answer, status, token, cost, and trace fields, not the persisted provider/model. Single-answer task construction instead starts from the persisted ReportAgent provider/model. The two replay paths therefore disagree about identity.
Recommended change
Choose and expose a replay contract: “repeat saved run” must use the saved model and effective inputs; “run with current settings” must create a new answer revision with matching provenance. Never write a response from a changed provider/model into a row retaining the old identity.
Verification to run after a fix
Acceptance: change a saved Agent’s model and provider after a completed report, exercise both regeneration paths, and assert the actual dispatched identity equals the saved/displayed identity and cost attribution.

P1R03

Several storage APIs acknowledge writes that failed

Persistence · Code defect · Source review; scenario not run end to end

An answer, edit, note, or imported report can appear successfully saved even when it will disappear on reload. New work may proceed without a durably created parent report.

Trigger / reproduction scenario
An atomic write returns false, for example because storage is full or a filesystem operation fails. Exercise create/update/note/import paths without injecting an exception higher in the stack.
Evidence and causal chain
ReportStorage.saveReport returns Unit and only logs a false writeTextAtomic result. updateAgentStatus returns true after calling it; persistNewReport also returns true after saveReport regardless of outcome. appendApiCallCosts returns an append result after the same unchecked writer. SecondaryResultStorage.save returns the supplied object even when a parent is absent or a write fails. The stronger saveAll and saveIfStillPresent contracts elsewhere prove the inconsistency is avoidable. Atomic replacement protects an old file; it does not prove that the new data reached disk.
Recommended change
Return an explicit write result through all mutations and their callers. Only publish success or dispatch dependent paid work after durable creation. Keep failed data available for retry and surface a recoverable save error. Ensure usage queues retain unacknowledged rows.
Verification to run after a fix
Acceptance: inject false atomic writes at parent creation, answer completion, note save, cost append, and import. No caller may claim persistence; the old file must remain readable and a later successful retry must preserve the new data exactly once.

P1R04

Turning off usage statistics also disables the Report cost ledger

Costs · Code defect · Source review; scenario not run end to end

New reports can have a ledger marked complete while it contains none of their paid calls. Ledger-derived totals then understate expenditure even though individual answer cost fields were updated.

Trigger / reproduction scenario
Disable the global usage-statistics switch, create a new report, and complete a response with priced usage. Re-enable statistics and reopen or reconcile the report.
Evidence and causal chain
SettingsPreferences.updateUsageStats returns before recordReportApiCallCost when usageStatsEnabled is false. New reports are created with apiCallCostsComplete=true and the current ledger version. computeReportTotalCost uses only that ledger for current reports. Reconciliation returns immediately for a current ledger, so re-enabling collection does not repair missing calls. The switch intentionally suppresses statistics, but “complete ledger” and normal report-cost presentation are incompatible with that suppression.
Recommended change
Decouple report accounting from optional aggregate usage statistics, or record an explicit incomplete/not-recorded state and show unavailable totals. Do not label a suppressed ledger complete. Define whether later repair is possible from retained answer/secondary usage.
Verification to run after a fix
Acceptance: run the same priced report with the statistics switch on and off. Either report accounting remains correct in both cases, or the disabled case clearly displays incomplete/unavailable costs and is eligible for appropriate reconciliation.

P2R05

The final usage batch has no scheduled flush

Costs · Code defect · Source review; scenario not run end to end

The last calls of a burst can remain only in memory for an unbounded idle period. A process kill can permanently lose their report ledger entries and aggregate statistics.

Trigger / reproduction scenario
Complete one call that flushes, then another within the two-second flush window, and stop making calls. Wait longer than two seconds, then let the process die without ViewModel.onCleared being delivered.
Evidence and causal chain
scheduleUsageStatsFlush checks elapsed time and returns inside the window; it does not schedule a delayed task. A future call or explicit flush is needed. The explicit lifecycle hook is AppViewModel.onCleared, which is not a guaranteed process-death callback. In addition, flushPendingReportApiCallCostsLocked clears pending rows before appending them, compounding R03 when a write fails. This is a leading-edge rate limit on writes, not a trailing-edge debounce.
Recommended change
Add a single scheduled trailing flush and durable acknowledgement/requeue semantics. For accounting that must survive abrupt termination, use a durable append journal or transactional outbox instead of relying solely on a lifecycle callback. Keep the chosen bounded-loss policy visible and documented.
Verification to run after a fix
Acceptance: two calls 100 ms apart followed by idle must both be on disk after the flush deadline, without a third call. Add failure/retry and abrupt-process-death cases, checking for neither omission nor duplication.

P2R06

Paid worker responses rejected by the parser disappear from accounting

Costs · Code defect · Source review; scenario not run end to end

A worker can consume provider tokens yet contribute no usage/cost record because its answer was not accepted as an artifact. A successful fallback then makes the batch look cheaper than the attempts it required.

Trigger / reproduction scenario
A judge returns HTTP 200 and token usage but malformed verdict JSON, or an icon/title worker returns usable text that lacks the required artifact. The pool falls through to another worker.
Evidence and causal chain
WorkerRunner only returns an accepted response as WorkerOutcome.Success; successful logical misses are logged and discarded. Its caller records the winner’s usage. The fixed-judge path returns Rejected before the updateUsageStatsAsync block when accepted(resp) is false. Transport success, artifact acceptance, and billable work are therefore coupled at the wrong boundary. Provider billing for failed transport/partial streams is additionally uncertain and needs reconciliation; this finding’s strongest proof is the successful response with explicit usage.
Recommended change
Account every response carrying billable usage before artifact validation, with an attempt/call ID and accepted/rejected outcome. Separately account transport failures when provider usage is known. Preserve costs without fabricating a successful analysis row.
Verification to run after a fix
Acceptance: a first worker returns 100/50 tokens and invalid output; a fallback returns 80/20 and valid output. The report ledger must contain both attempts while the analysis row points only to the accepted result.

P2R07

Deleting a saved Agent can strand full regeneration

Regeneration · Code defect · Source review; scenario not run end to end

A persisted answer whose provider still exists but whose Agent was deleted can be reset to pending without receiving a replacement call. The batch can wait until its 30-minute safety timeout.

Trigger / reproduction scenario
Generate with a saved Agent, delete that Agent from settings, and start a full regenerate batch. A similar state can occur after importing a report whose Agents are absent on the destination.
Evidence and causal chain
The batch creates an AGENTS task with the original agentId whenever its provider resolves. reportToModels falls back to a direct model for a missing Agent; that direct model receives a synthetic swarm:provider:model result ID. forceRegenerateAllAgents filters built tasks using the original onlyAgentIds. The fallback task is removed by that filter, but resetRowsForPhase already reset the original row. Provider-resolution guards address a different missing-provider case and do not address this ID mismatch.
Recommended change
Carry the original result ID through orphan fallback construction. If a row truly cannot run, exclude it before reset and persist a specific skipped/unavailable reason. Use the same resolver for planning, dispatch, and completion tracking.
Verification to run after a fix
Acceptance: remove an Agent but retain its provider and key. Full regeneration must either regenerate that original answer correctly or skip it immediately with a visible reason; it must not wait for the timeout.

P1R08

Saved runs lack immutable effective configuration

Reproducibility · Code defect · Source review; scenario not run end to end

Regeneration and resumed evaluations can mix different prompts, parameters, and worker choices under one historical report/run. A stored prompt ID is not a snapshot of the prompt that was used.

Trigger / reproduction scenario
Run with a report-level system prompt or preset, edit that saved object, then regenerate. Separately launch a tournament with a run-only edited rubric or temperature, kill/restart the process, and retry a cell.
Evidence and causal chain
Report records preset/system-prompt IDs and selection IDs; regeneration resolves their current contents. It also reads live externalSystemPrompt. Tournament/Compare keep run-only prompt text in live state, while disk rows primarily retain prompt ID/name. Hydration can recover the current saved prompt rather than the prior effective text. Tournament hydrate preserves a live prompt but reconstructs TournamentRunState without runParams, losing its live temperature override; the dispatch comment also explicitly acknowledges null runParams after process death.
Recommended change
Persist a versioned execution manifest per run: resolved system/user templates, effective non-secret parameters, selected workers/models/endpoints, source revisions, and capability-filter decisions. Store credential references only. Make “replay saved settings” and “use current settings” explicit operations.
Verification to run after a fix
Acceptance: mutate every referenced configuration after a run and verify a saved replay remains identical at the request-construction boundary. Retry before/after hydration and process death with a run-only rubric/temperature; the same run must retain them.

P1R09

Analyses and translations are not bound to answer revisions

Reproducibility · Code defect · Source review; scenario not run end to end

An old verdict can be shown alongside a newly edited answer as though it evaluates that text. Translation judges can compare an old translation against a different, current original.

Trigger / reproduction scenario
Generate an answer, translate/rerank/compare it, then replace its response through chat refinement or model-only regeneration. Open the old evaluation or run translator ranking on the old translation.
Evidence and causal chain
applyAgentChatResponse overwrites responseBody and change-source fields without creating an immutable answer revision or invalidating dependent results. sourceAgentResponses joins saved IDs to current response bodies. TranslatorRankEngine.originalTextFor reads the current answer/meta text for a stored translation. sourceAgentIds preserves participant identity but not the evaluated content. The old trace, token counts, duration, and other response metadata can also remain alongside the replacement text.
Recommended change
Introduce answerRevisionId/content hash and preserve original response metadata per revision. Every secondary should reference immutable source revisions. Mark derived results stale after replacement, retain historical drill-in, and offer an explicit refresh of selected dependents.
Verification to run after a fix
Acceptance: translate “The meeting is Monday,” replace the source with “The meeting is Tuesday,” then rank the saved translation. It must be evaluated against Monday’s saved revision or rejected as stale, never silently compared with Tuesday.

P2R10

Batch recovery redoes successful work and cancellation leaves calls running

Regeneration · Workflow contract · Source review; scenario not run end to end

A small metadata failure can block answer regeneration; “Restart” can repeat successful siblings and spend again. “Cancel” stops scheduling but does not stop already dispatched calls or their subsequent writes.

Trigger / reproduction scenario
Start full regeneration with metadata phases enabled. Let an icon/title fail, or let one answer fail after another succeeds. Choose Restart, Skip, or Cancel while other calls are still in flight.
Evidence and causal chain
RegeneratePhase places TITLE/ICON/LANGUAGE before AGENTS. The orchestrator pauses on the first error and resets every task in the current phase on restart, including prior successes. The detail UI says to fix the row and tap Restart. cancel explicitly cancels only the orchestrator and allows in-flight HTTP calls to finish/persist. These are concrete current semantics; old/new attempt overlap is an additional race scenario to verify, not a reproduced race in this audit.
Recommended change
Let optional enrichment fail independently of primary answers. Offer “retry failed/unfinished” as the normal recovery, with an explicit rerun-whole-phase action. Either cascade cancellation into owned jobs or label it “Stop scheduling” and show in-flight work. Fence late writes by attempt revision.
Verification to run after a fix
Acceptance: one failure among three tasks must not replay the two successes under a retry-failed action. Cancel must match the displayed promise. An older in-flight attempt must not mark a restarted attempt complete or overwrite its later answer.

analyzeJudges computes per-match consensus from ALL verdicts and then compares each contributing judge with that consensus. consensusForMatch maps split/no-unique-A-or-B outcomes to tie. Trigger / reproduction scenario

SelectWorkers exposes worker routing and parameter cards; engines have useful planned-count helpers, including N(N−1) tournament calls and capped translator-judge cells. These mechanisms are distributed. Regeneration can also replay a full phase (R10), and worker fallback attempts are additional work. No universal dollar estimate can be exact before outputs are known, so an honest range and explicit unknowns are preferable to false precision.
Recommended change
Build a shared resolved execution plan used by both preview and dispatch. Show primary calls, optional enrichment, sources × responders × judges, retry/fallback policy, known pricing, estimated range, and an optional spending/work cap. Make narrow translation of selected content easy before broad whole-report translation.
Verification to run after a fix
Acceptance: preview counts match actual initially scheduled work for each operation, invalid/empty scopes cannot broaden, and retry/fallback work is distinguished from the initial plan. Unknown prices remain unknown.

Observed Report screens

These screenshots document the installed app’s observed configuration. They support the navigation and identity observations; they do not reproduce the storage, replay, or scoring defects. No new AI requests were launched. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

An early UI hierarchy briefly showed incomplete totals while loading. The settled Manage screen was used for the audit; the loading snapshot was not reported as a cost bug.

Implementation order

Repair integrity before adding analysis depth

Close the immediate correctness gaps

Fix rerank ID joins (R01), prevent model relabeling on replay (R02), propagate durable-write outcomes (R03), and make suppressed accounting explicit (R04). Add narrowly targeted fault/identity checks. Apply safe export transformation at the bundle boundary (R15).

Make runs and costs durable

Implement immutable answer revisions and an execution manifest (R08–R09). Give each call/attempt a stable accounting ID, record rejected paid responses, and flush/acknowledge queued costs reliably (R05–R06). Preserve a clear distinction between historical spend and the currently displayed answer (R25).

Unify planning, recovery, and scope resolution

Use the same resolved task IDs for preview, reset, dispatch, and completion (R07). Retry only intended work, fence late writes, and define cancellation precisely (R10). Empty scopes must remain empty (R11). Make import staging and copy semantics explicit (R16–R17).

Align controls with actual requests

Resolve local/worker settings deliberately, retain selected-group provenance, and support or explicitly reject distinct same-model variants (R12–R13, R18–R19). Persist retrieval evidence and degraded-mode status (R14).

Make comparisons interpretable and scale from measurements

Explain score meaning and coverage, remove unsupported ratio claims, avoid double-weighting the same tournament evidence, and distinguish translation review from benchmarking (R20–R24). Then profile large workloads (R26) and improve the reading/launch experience (R27–R28).

Suggested data invariant: a displayed answer refers to one immutable answer revision; an evaluation names the exact source revisions and effective rubric; a call ledger names every acknowledged billable attempt; a UI “saved” state corresponds to a successful durable write.

This can be introduced incrementally. It does not require a wholesale database migration before fixing the immediate identity joins and write acknowledgements.

Work still needed to verify fixes

A targeted validation backlog

The repository has existing helper, storage, redaction, concurrency, and Compose tests. The next useful step is to test the cross-layer invariants that connect those components. Run the extended cycle only when explicitly requested, following the repository’s app-data preservation procedure before instrumentation.

Small deterministic examples

  • Score identity: [A:90, B:60, C:20] minus A must produce [B:60, C:20], not [B:90, C:60].
  • Value scale: 100/1 < 200/1.5, but 1100/1 > 1200/1.5. A score offset can flip the ratio winner.
  • Self-agreement: one judge’s verdict is its own consensus, yielding 100% whenever a verdict exists.
  • Work multiplication: 100 × 99 = 9,900 oriented tournament matches before additional judging/retries.

These are reasoning fixtures illustrating the code paths, not executed application test results.

Acceptance criteria for an audit follow-up

  • Every fixed finding has a request/disk/UI invariant appropriate to the defect.
  • Fault tests verify behavior across component boundaries, not just helper output.
  • UI claims state source, coverage, revision, and cost uncertainty when relevant.
  • Data migration preserves existing report bodies, notes, spend history, and valid links.
  • A fresh installed build receives a focused functional walkthrough after the relevant fixes.
Balanced assessment

Safeguards that should be preserved

Existing strengths

  • Atomic file replacement and locked read-modify-write protect existing data from torn or stale whole-object writes.
  • Flat-ID/canonical containment checks protect report and secondary filesystem boundaries.
  • Secondary saveAll and saveIfStillPresent provide stronger acknowledgement/deletion protection than the weaker paths called out in R03.
  • Shared batch machinery, persisted placeholders, item job tracking, and report-owned deletion guards address many cancellation/navigation hazards.
  • Provider/global concurrency controls and throttled scheduling are substantial. Report log contexts use Dispatchers.IO; this audit does not claim all Report I/O runs on Main.
  • Current trace capture masks standard API secrets; readable exports apply additional redaction. Import remaps report, secondary, run, trace, and many note/reference identities.
  • Current Value code excludes unknown prices from best-value candidacy, avoids unknown-price domination, remaps tournament participants, and drops flat Combined sources.
  • Translator sampling is deterministic. Knowledge retrieval skips incompatible embeddings instead of scoring them. These fixes narrow, but do not eliminate, the findings above.

Suspicions not promoted to findings

  • Universal plaintext credential export: rejected for standard current traces; R15 describes the verified weaker bundle boundary and imported/legacy cases.
  • Generic model-output HTML execution: no blanket XSS claim. Export escaping and preview restrictions were observed; bypass testing was not performed.
  • Every missing JSON list causes a crash: rejected as a general claim because app Gson normalizes missing/null collections. Import transaction/acknowledgement issues remain.
  • Flat Combined sources distort current rankings: current code explicitly drops them; the remaining issue is coverage/calibration and correlated evidence.
  • KnowledgeService compares incompatible embeddings: current code skips mismatches; the remaining issue is invisible loss of context.
  • Zero costs in the initial emulator load: settled data replaced the transient initial values.
  • All report work is lost on navigation: app/view-model job ownership and background paths make that claim too broad. This audit isolates specific recovery failures instead.

Documentation maintenance

The earlier functional audit remains useful for product semantics. This review independently follows current implementation paths and adds technical failure chains. Some source comments lag fixes: runtime trace masking contradicts the “unredacted” export-helper comment, and the chat-response replacement comment understates current report-scoped accounting intent. The top-level file/line inventory is also below the current measured tree. Update comments alongside behavior so future reviews do not mistake old diagnoses for current defects.

Key orientation documents: architecture, state ownership, development cycle, regeneration, secondary results, tournament/judges/Compare, Value, parameters, and backup/restore.
